5:The service is intended to grow around attestation formats, verifier trust roots, nonce and freshness controls, policy evaluation, confidential data envelopes, one-time release grants, workload identity, revocation, audit evidence, key rotation, tenant isolation, rate limits, failure recovery, and operational observability. Every release decision must remain explainable and auditable without exposing the protected payload or private key material.
16:uvicorn proof_release.app:app --reload
22:- `POST /v1/challenges/{challenge_id}/consume` consumes a pending, unexpired challenge by presenting its nonce to prove freshness.
23:- `POST /v1/evidence` receives attestation evidence for a pending, unexpired challenge. The JSON body must include `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `challenge_id`, `nonce` (unpadded base64url), `evidence_format`, and `evidence`. On success it returns `201` with `evidence_id`, `challenge_id`, status `received`, and a UTC RFC3339 `received_at`, and consumes the challenge in the same transaction so it cannot be reused. Only the SHA-256 digest of the evidence is persisted — never the evidence itself. Errors: `404` unknown/mismatched challenge, `401` wrong nonce, `409` already consumed or received, `410` expired, `422` invalid fields.
26:- `POST /v1/policies` creates a versioned release policy scoped to a tenant and workload. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `name` and `rule`. A rule is exactly one of `{"claim": "<top-level claim name>", "equals": <scalar>}` (scalar = string, number, boolean or null), `{"all": [rule, ...]}`, `{"any": [rule, ...]}` (both non-empty lists) or `{"not": rule}`; any other shape is rejected with `422`. Creating a policy with an existing `(tenant_id, workload_id, name)` allocates the next integer `version` (the first is `1`) and retains every older version unchanged; scope or name isolation restarts the sequence at `1`. Concurrent creators never share or skip a version. On success it returns `201` with `policy_id`, the scope, `name`, `version`, the submitted `rule`, and a UTC RFC3339 `created_at`. Policies are persisted and survive restarts; only the rule tree (claim names and expected scalars — never evidence or claim values) is stored.
27:- `POST /v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/decisions` evaluates a verified piece of evidence against one policy version and records an auditable release decision. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `nonce` (unpadded base64url), `evidence` (the same bytes received/verified — checked by SHA-256 digest, never re-verified and never persisted) and `policy_id`. Both the evidence and the policy must belong to exactly the request's tenant and workload (`404` if either is unknown or cross-scope), the evidence must already be settled `verified` (`409` for received or rejected evidence), the nonce must match the evidence's bound challenge, the evidence digest must match, and the evidence format must be one of the built-in JSON formats whose `claims` the service can read (`422` otherwise). The rule is evaluated against the top-level `claims` of the digest-matched evidence; a satisfied rule yields status `allowed`, anything else (including a missing claim) yields `denied` — both return `200` with `decision_id`, `evidence_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_version`, `status` and a UTC RFC3339 `decided_at`. Exactly one audit decision exists per evidence and policy version: retries and concurrent requests return the identical stored result. The audit row stores only identifiers, the fixed status code and timestamps — never the raw evidence, the nonce, or the evaluated claims.
28:- `POST /v1/release-grants` mints a one-time, TTL-bounded release grant on top of an existing decision. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `decision_id` and `data_id`, plus an optional integer `ttl_seconds` (30–900, default 300). Only a decision whose scope is exactly the request's tenant and workload can be referenced (`404` if unknown or cross-scope), and only an `allowed` decision can authorize a grant (`409` for any other status; invalid fields return `422`). On success it returns `201` with `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, a cryptographically random `capability` (32 bytes, unpadded base64url), `pending: true`, and UTC RFC3339 `issued_at`/`expires_at`. The capability is returned exactly once, on this response: only its SHA-256 digest is persisted, it is never logged, and it never appears on any other response. Multiple grants may be minted for the same decision/data item; each is independent. A pending grant settles exactly once: it is either consumed (via the consume endpoint or a successful payload release) or revoked (via the revoke endpoint below), whichever valid request wins the shared atomic transition first.
29:- `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/consume` consumes a pending, unexpired grant by presenting its capability. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id` and `capability` (`422` otherwise; a syntactically invalid path grant id is `422` as well). An unknown or cross-scope grant returns `404`, a wrong capability returns `401` (without settling the grant), an already-consumed or already-revoked grant returns `409`, and an expired grant returns `410` (a settled grant reports `409` even after its expiry). On success it returns `200` with exactly `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, `consumed: true` and a UTC RFC3339 `consumed_at`. The pending → consumed transition is a single guarded update shared with the revoke and payload-release endpoints, so concurrent consumers race: exactly one succeeds and the rest receive `409` (a request that loses to a revocation observes `409 grant already revoked`), with no extra audit rows; grants are persisted and survive restarts. The audit row stores only the grant/decision identifiers, the scope, the data identifier, the fixed status, timestamps, and the capability digest — never the plaintext capability, evidence, claims, or any payload.
30:- `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/revoke` revokes a still-pending, unexpired grant by presenting its capability. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id` and `capability`; a missing, blank, wrong-typed or malformed field, or a syntactically invalid path grant id (including an empty path segment), returns `422` and writes no state. Judgements are made in a fixed order: an unknown grant, or one belonging to another tenant or workload, returns `404` (an unknown-but-well-formed path identifier is the same indistinguishable `404`); a wrong capability returns `401` and changes no state — the grant stays pending, so an erroneous capability can never revoke, consume or otherwise alter it; a grant already consumed or already revoked returns `409`; and an expired grant that is still pending returns `410`, with the status judgement always preceding the write. A valid request atomically settles pending → `revoked` and returns `200` with exactly `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, `revoked: true` and a UTC RFC3339 `revoked_at`; the plaintext capability is never echoed. Repeating the revoke returns `409` and rewrites neither `revoked_at` nor any audit. app = FastAPI(title="Remote Attestation Data Release")

    def _scope_budget_acquire(
        tenant_id: str, workload_id: str, now: datetime
    ) -> bool:
        """Consume one unit of the scope's per-minute request budget.

        Returns ``True`` when the request is admitted (its budget unit is
        committed before this returns, regardless of the request's later
        outcome) and ``False`` when the scope's current UTC-minute window
        is already full. The counter lives in the database, so the budget
        is shared by the consume/revoke/release endpoints, across
        processes, and survives restarts. The guarded increment plus the
        (scope, window) primary key make concurrent acquisitions exact:
        more than RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE simultaneous valid requests admit
        exactly RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE winners.
        """
        window_minute = int(now.timestamp() // 60)
        increment = (
            update(RateLimitWindow)
            .where(
                RateLimitWindow.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                RateLimitWindow.workload_id == workload_id,
                RateLimitWindow.window_minute == window_minute,
                RateLimitWindow.used < RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE,
            )
            .values(used=RateLimitWindow.used + 1)
            .execution_options(synchronize_session=False)
        )
        with session_factory() as session:
            result = session.execute(increment)
            if result.rowcount == 1:
                session.commit()
                return True
            session.rollback()
        # No row for this window yet (or it is already full). Try to open
        # the window; the primary key rejects the insert if a concurrent
        # request created the row first.
        with session_factory() as session:
            session.add(
                RateLimitWindow(
                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
                    workload_id=workload_id,
                    window_minute=window_minute,
                    used=1,
                )
            )
            try:
                session.commit()
                return True
            except IntegrityError:
                session.rollback()
        # A concurrent request opened the window first; take a slot from
        # it. If this also misses, the window is genuinely full.
        with session_factory() as session:
            result = session.execute(increment)
            if result.rowcount == 1:
                session.commit()
                return True
            session.rollback()
        return False

    def _rate_limited_response(now: datetime) -> Response:
        """Compact 429 body: only the whole seconds left in the window.

        ``retry_after_seconds`` is the number of full seconds until the
        current UTC minute window closes — always a positive integer in
        [1, 60], never a float. Repeating a limited request changes
        nothing: no budget is consumed and the window is not extended.
        """
        retry_after = 60 - now.second
        body = (
            json.dumps(
                {"retry_after_seconds": retry_after},
                separators=(",", ":"),
                allow_nan=False,
            ).encode("utf-8")
            + b"\n"
        )
        return Response(
            content=body, status_code=429, media_type="application/json"
        )

def test_concurrent_settlement_then_replay_remains_stable(app):
    client = TestClient(app)
    decision = _decision(client)
    grants = [_mint(client, decision["decision_id"], data_id=f"d{i}") for i in range(6)]

    import proof_release.app as app_module

    app_module.AUDIT_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE = 3
    try:
        first = _query(client).json()
        assert first["complete"] is False
        cursor = first["next_cursor"]
        second_before = _query(client, cursor=cursor).json()
        second_keys = [
            (row["occurred_at"], row["event_id"]) for row in second_before["events"]
        ]
        assert len(second_keys) == 3

        def settle(index):
            local = TestClient(app)
            grant = grants[index]
            path = (
                f"/v1/release-grants/{grant['grant_id']}/"
                + ("consume" if index % 2 == 0 else "revoke")
            )
            response = local.post(
                path,
                json={"tenant_id": TENANT, "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
                      "capability": grant["capability"]},
            )
            assert response.status_code == 200

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
            list(pool.map(settle, range(6)))

        # Replaying the cursor returns the identical page of pre-existing
        # events; newly committed settlement events appear only on later
        # pages, never duplicating or shifting the replayed page.
        second_after = _query(client, cursor=cursor).json()
        assert (
            [(row["occurred_at"], row["event_id"]) for row in second_after["events"]]
            == second_keys
        )

        # A full walk sees every event once in stable order.
        all_rows = []
        token = None
        for _ in range(20):
            data = _query(client, **({"cursor": token} if token else {})).json()
            all_rows.extend(data["events"])
            if data["complete"]:
                break
            token = data["next_cursor"]
        keys = [(row["occurred_at"], row["event_id"]) for row in all_rows]
        assert keys == sorted(keys)
        assert len(keys) == 12  # 6 pending + 6 settlement events
        assert len({key[1] for key in keys}) == 12
    finally:
        app_module.AUDIT_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE = 100

input.content:
"""Tests for the per-scope per-minute admission budget.

The release-grant consume, revoke and payload-release endpoints share a
budget of five field-valid requests per (tenant, workload) scope and UTC
minute. Requests that fail field validation (422) never consume budget;
every syntactically valid, scoped request consumes exactly one unit
regardless of its business outcome (404/401/409/410/500). The sixth
valid request in the same window is rejected with 429 and a compact
``retry_after_seconds`` body, writing no state and no audit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

import proof_release.app as app_module
from proof_release.app import create_app
from proof_release.db import AuditEvent, ReleaseGrant
from proof_release.envelopes import b64url_encode

TENANT = "tenant-a"
WORKLOAD = "workload-1"
OTHER_TENANT = "tenant-b"
OTHER_WORKLOAD = "workload-2"
DATA_ID = "data-1"
SECRET = "unit-test-secret"
MASTER_KEY = b64url_encode(b"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
PAYLOAD = "rate limited secret payload"

#: A well-formed capability that matches nothing.
UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY = "A" * 43
#: A well-formed grant identifier that matches nothing.
UNKNOWN_GRANT = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"


@pytest.fixture()
def clock(monkeypatch):
    """A controllable UTC clock, started on a minute boundary."""
    box = {"now": datetime(2026, 1, 5, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)}
    monkeypatch.setattr(app_module, "_utcnow", lambda: box["now"])
    return box


@pytest.fixture()
def app(tmp_path, monkeypatch, clock):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PROOF_RELEASE_ATTESTED_NONCE_SECRET", SECRET)
    monkeypatch.setenv("PROOF_RELEASE_MASTER_KEY", MASTER_KEY)
    application = create_app(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path}/rate.db")
    yield application
    application.state.engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture()
def client(app):
    return TestClient(app)


def _mac(nonce: str, claims: dict) -> str:
    key = hmac.new(
        SECRET.encode("utf-8"),
        f"{TENANT}:{WORKLOAD}".encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).digest()
    payload = json.dumps(
        {"claims": claims, "nonce": nonce},
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return hmac.new(key, payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def _evidence(nonce: str) -> str:
    claims = {"m": "x"}
    return json.dumps({"nonce": nonce, "claims": claims, "mac": _mac(nonce, claims)})


def _decision(client, tenant=TENANT, workload=WORKLOAD):
    created = client.post(
        "/v1/challenges", json={"tenant_id": tenant, "workload_id": workload}
    ).json()
    evidence = _evidence(created["nonce"])
    submitted = client.post(
        "/v1/evidence",
        json={
            "tenant_id": tenant,
            "workload_id": workload,
            "challenge_id": created["challenge_id"],
            "nonce": created["nonce"],
            "evidence_format": "attested-nonce-json",
            "evidence": evidence,
        },
    )
    assert submitted.status_code == 201
    evidence_id = submitted.json()["evidence_id"]
    verified = client.post(
        f"/v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/verify",
        json={
            "tenant_id": tenant,
            "workload_id": workload,
            "nonce": created["nonce"],
            "evidence": evidence,
        },
    )
    assert verified.status_code == 200
    policy = client.post(
        "/v1/policies",
        json={
            "tenant_id": tenant,
            "workload_id": workload,
            "name": "release",
            "rule": {"claim": "m", "equals": "x"},
        },
    ).json()
    decided = client.post(
        f"/v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/decisions",
        json={
            "tenant_id": tenant,
            "workload_id": workload,
            "nonce": created["nonce"],
            "evidence": evidence,
            "policy_id": policy["policy_id"],
        },
    )
    assert decided.status_code == 200
    return decided.json()


def _envelope(client, data_id=DATA_ID, payload=PAYLOAD):
    response = client.post(
        "/v1/data-envelopes",
        json={
            "tenant_id": TENANT,
            "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
            "data_id": data_id,
            "payload": payload,
        },
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201
    return response.json()


def _grant(client, decision_id, data_id=DATA_ID, **fields):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "decision_id": decision_id,
        "data_id": data_id,
    }
    body.update(fields)
    response = client.post("/v1/release-grants", json=body)
    assert response.status_code == 201
    return response.json()


def _consume(client, grant_id=UNKNOWN_GRANT, capability=UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY, **fields):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "capability": capability,
    }
    body.update(fields)
    return client.post(f"/v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/consume", json=body)


def _revoke(client, grant_id=UNKNOWN_GRANT, capability=UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY, **fields):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "capability": capability,
    }
    body.update(fields)
    return client.post(f"/v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/revoke", json=body)


def _release(client, grant_id=UNKNOWN_GRANT, capability=UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY, **fields):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "data_id": DATA_ID,
        "capability": capability,
    }
    body.update(fields)
    return client.post(f"/v1/release/{grant_id}", json=body)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Admission and budget accounting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_five_valid_requests_admitted_sixth_limited(client):
    # Unknown grants: every request is syntactically valid and scoped, so
    # each consumes one budget unit even though the outcome is 404.
    for _ in range(5):
        assert _consume(client).status_code == 404
    response = _consume(client)
    assert response.status_code == 429


def test_every_business_outcome_consumes_budget(client, clock):
    decision = _decision(client)
    grant = _grant(client, decision["decision_id"])
    # 200: a winning consume.
    assert _consume(client, grant["grant_id"], grant["capability"]).status_code == 200
    # 409: the same grant is now settled.
    assert _consume(client, grant["grant_id"], grant["capability"]).status_code == 409
    # 401: a well-formed but wrong capability on a fresh grant.
    other = _grant(client, decision["decision_id"])
    assert _consume(client, other["grant_id"]).status_code == 401
    # 404: an unknown grant.
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 404
    # 410: a grant minted with the minimum TTL, observed after expiry but
    # within the same UTC minute window.
    expiring = _grant(client, decision["decision_id"], ttl_seconds=30)
    clock["now"] += timedelta(seconds=31)
    assert _consume(client, expiring["grant_id"], expiring["capability"]).status_code == 410
    # The sixth valid request in the window is limited.
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 429


def test_server_error_outcome_consumes_budget(app, client):
    decision = _decision(client)
    _envelope(client)
    grant = _grant(client, decision["decision_id"])
    # Corrupt the envelope so every release attempt fails decryption with
    # a 500 while the grant stays pending.
    with app.state.session_factory() as session:
        from proof_release.db import DataEnvelope

        envelope = session.get(DataEnvelope, (TENANT, WORKLOAD, DATA_ID))
        tampered = bytearray(envelope.ciphertext)
        tampered[0] ^= 0x01
        envelope.ciphertext = bytes(tampered)
        session.commit()

    for _ in range(5):
        response = _release(client, grant["grant_id"], grant["capability"])
        assert response.status_code == 500
    assert _release(client, grant["grant_id"], grant["capability"]).status_code == 429


def test_budget_shared_across_consume_revoke_and_release(client):
    _decision(client)
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 404
    assert _revoke(client).status_code == 404
    assert _release(client).status_code == 404
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 404
    assert _revoke(client).status_code == 404
    # The five admissions are spent across the three endpoints; the next
    # valid request on any of them is limited.
    assert _release(client).status_code == 429
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 429
    assert _revoke(client).status_code == 429


def test_budget_is_strictly_per_scope(client):
    for _ in range(5):
        assert _consume(client).status_code == 404
    assert _consume(client).status_code == 429

28	- `POST /v1/release-grants` mints a one-time, TTL-bounded release grant on top of an existing decision. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `decision_id` and `data_id`, plus an optional integer `ttl_seconds` (30–900, default 300). Only a decision whose scope is exactly the request's tenant and workload can be referenced (`404` if unknown or cross-scope), and only an `allowed` decision can authorize a grant (`409` for any other status; invalid fields return `422`). On success it returns `201` with `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, a cryptographically random `capability` (32 bytes, unpadded base64url), `pending: true`, and UTC RFC3339 `issued_at`/`expires_at`. The capability is returned exactly once, on this response: only its SHA-256 digest is persisted, it is never logged, and it never appears on any other response. Multiple grants may be minted for the same decision/data item; each is independent. A pending grant settles exactly once: it is either consumed (via the consume endpoint or a successful payload release) or revoked (via the revoke endpoint below), whichever valid request wins the shared atomic transition first.
29	- `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/consume` consumes a pending, unexpired grant by presenting its capability. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id` and `capability` (`422` otherwise; a syntactically invalid path grant id is `422` as well). An unknown or cross-scope grant returns `404`, a wrong capability returns `401` (without settling the grant), an already-consumed or already-revoked grant returns `409`, and an expired grant returns `410` (a settled grant reports `409` even after its expiry). On success it returns `200` with exactly `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, `consumed: true` and a UTC RFC3339 `consumed_at`. The pending → consumed transition is a single guarded update shared with the revoke and payload-release endpoints, so concurrent consumers race: exactly one succeeds and the rest receive `409` (a request that loses to a revocation observes `409 grant already revoked`), with no extra audit rows; grants are persisted and survive restarts. The audit row stores only the grant/decision identifiers, the scope, the data identifier, the fixed status, timestamps, and the capability digest — never the plaintext capability, evidence, claims, or any payload.
30	- `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/revoke` revokes a still-pending, unexpired grant by presenting its capability. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id` and `capability`; a missing, blank, wrong-typed or malformed field, or a syntactically invalid path grant id (including an empty path segment), returns `422` and writes no state. Judgements are made in a fixed order: an unknown grant, or one belonging to another tenant or workload, returns `404` (an unknown-but-well-formed path identifier is the same indistinguishable `404`); a wrong capability returns `401` and changes no state — the grant stays pending, so an erroneous capability can never revoke, consume or otherwise alter it; a grant already consumed or already revoked returns `409`; and an expired grant that is still pending returns `410`, with the status judgement always preceding the write. A valid request atomically settles pending → `revoked` and returns `200` with exactly `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, `revoked: true` and a UTC RFC3339 `revoked_at`; the plaintext capability is never echoed. Repeating the revoke returns `409` and rewrites neither `revoked_at` nor any audit. Revocation shares the grant's single guarded atomic transition with the consume endpoint and `POST /v1/release/{grant_id}`: of all valid concurrent revoke/consume/release requests at most one wins, and every loser only observes the final state as `409` — when revocation wins, a subsequent or losing consume and release both return `409` and release produces no payload and no extra audit row. Revocation is scoped to the single grant; other grants (including other grants for the same data item) are untouched. The audit record is the grant row itself, recording only the grant/decision/data identifiers, the scope, the fixed status, timestamps and the capability SHA-256 digest — never the plaintext capability, payload, data key, evidence or claims, on any response, in storage or in logs.
31	- `POST /v1/release/{grant_id}` releases the protected payload authorized by a one-time grant, connecting the grant to its data envelope. The path identifier must identify the same grant; the JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id`, `workload_id`, `data_id` and `capability` (`422` for any missing, blank, wrong-typed, malformed or otherwise invalid field). Judgements are made in a fixed order: an unknown grant, an unknown or cross-scope data item, or a `data_id` different from the one the grant was minted for returns `404` (and writes no consumption audit); a wrong capability returns `401` with the grant left pending; an expired grant returns `410` (whether or not it was later consumed or revoked); and only after those checks does an already-consumed or already-revoked grant return `409`. Before any state changes, the data key is unwrapped with the master key version recorded on the envelope and the payload is authenticated-decrypted (AES Key Wrap + AES-256-GCM). An invalid keyring, a missing historical key version, damaged wrapping material, or any other decryption failure returns `500` and leaves the grant pending with no consumption audit — only authenticated-decryption success commits the one-time state. The endpoint shares the grant's atomic pending → consumed state with the consume and revoke endpoints above, so concurrent or duplicate valid release/consume/revoke requests have exactly one winner; losers receive `409` (a loser to revocation gets `409 grant already revoked` and never decrypts or releases the payload) and each successful release produces exactly one audit row (scope, data identifier, status, timestamp and capability digest) that survives restarts. On success it returns `200` with compact JSON containing exactly one non-empty string field, `payload`, terminated by a single newline; the response carries no floats, `-0.0`, non-finite values or other metadata, and the capability is used only for verification and never echoed. The plaintext payload, plaintext capability and key material are never persisted, logged, or returned on any other response, and raw certificate material never enters logs.
32	- `GET /v1/release-grants` is the read-only authorization-lifecycle audit: it lists release grants for one tenant/workload in stable `grant_id` ascending order with keyset pagination; the request body is always empty. `tenant_id` and `workload_id` are required non-empty query parameters. Results may be narrowed by `grant_id` or `decision_id` (canonical UUIDs), by `data_id` (any non-empty caller-chosen identifier), by `status` (exactly `pending`, `consumed` or `revoked`), and by an inclusive issuance window `issued_after`/`issued_before`, both explicit UTC RFC3339 timestamps (`Z` or `+00:00`; a naive or non-UTC offset is rejected); `issued_after` must not be later than `issued_before`. A missing/blank/whitespace/typed-wrong field, an illegal identifier or status format, an illegal timestamp, or an inverted window returns `422` and writes no state. An explicit `grant_id`, `decision_id` or `data_id` that is unknown, belongs to another tenant/workload, or (for `data_id`) is referenced by neither an envelope nor any grant in the scope returns `404`. Pagination is cursor-driven: omitting `cursor` or sending an explicit empty string starts before the smallest grant id; the compact JSON response is exactly `grants`, `next_cursor` (empty at the end) and `complete`. Cursors are opaque, HMAC-authenticated tokens carrying a kind tag and bound to the scope *and* every active filter — a forged, tampered, cross-scope or cross-filter cursor returns `422` — so replaying the same cursor always returns the identical page in the identical order, never duplicating or skipping an entry. Each entry contains the JSON-string `grant_id`, `decision_id`, `data_id`, the fixed `status`, `capability_sha256` (the SHA-256 digest only), and UTC RFC3339 or `null` `issued_at`, `expires_at`, `consumed_at` and `revoked_at`. The plaintext capability, payloads, evidence, key and certificate material never appear; the response is compact JSON with no floats, `-0.0` or non-finite values. The handler issues only reads, never writes or settles state, and returns no half page: a storage/service failure is a `500` with no partial result. Concurrent consume/revoke transitions are unaffected; a query observes only committed state, and a replayed cursor keeps its stable order across such transitions. Audit rows persist across restarts.
33	- `GET /v1/compliance/audit-events` is the read-only compliance audit: it lists append-only audit events for one tenant/workload in stable `(occurred_at, event_id)` ascending order with keyset pagination; the request body is always empty and no other query parameters are accepted. `tenant_id` and `workload_id` are required non-empty query parameters. Results may be narrowed by `event_id` (a canonical UUID), `event_type` (exactly `grant` or `rewrap`), `status` (exactly `pending`, `consumed`, `revoked`, `rewrapped` or `skipped`), and by an inclusive window `occurred_after`/`occurred_before`, both explicit UTC RFC3339 timestamps (`Z` or `+00:00`; a naive or non-UTC offset is rejected); `occurred_after` must not be later than `occurred_before`. Set it outside local development, and keep it stable across restarts so previously issued cursors remain replayable (a changed secret simply makes outstanding cursors unrecognizable — clients restart from the beginning of the scope, which only yields skips for already-current envelopes). The read-only release-grant audit and compliance audit-event cursors use the same secret and HMAC construction, each tagged with its own cursor kind and bound to its full filter set, so no cursor family can ever be replayed against another endpoint and neither audit cursor can cross scopes or filter conditions.


### Verifier plugins

Formats are verified through a public plugin interface in `proof_release.verifiers`: implement `Verifier` (set `format_name` and `verify(context) -> VerificationResult`) and register it via `register_verifier()` on `default_registry`, or pass a custom `VerifierRegistry` to `create_app(..., verifier_registry=...)`. The verifier receives a `VerificationContext` containing the raw evidence for this call plus the tenant, workload and challenge context; the service layer never stores the raw evidence.

### Rate limits

The three authorization-action endpoints — `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/consume`, `POST /v1/release-grants/{grant_id}/revoke` and `POST /v1/release/{grant_id}` — share one admission budget per `(tenant_id, workload_id)` scope: at most five field-valid requests per UTC minute window, counted strictly by the scope named in the request body, so different tenants and workloads never affect each other. A request that fails field validation (missing, blank, wrong-typed or malformed fields, or an illegal scope/path identifier — all `422`) never consumes budget. Every syntactically valid, scoped request consumes exactly one unit the moment it is admitted, whatever its later business outcome (`200`, `404`, `401`, `409`, `410` or `500`). The sixth valid request within the same scope and minute — concurrent or serial — is rejected with `429` before any lookup, decryption, state change or audit write: the grant, its capability and the audit trail are exactly as if the request had never arrived. The `429` body is compact JSON containing exactly one field, `retry_after_seconds` — a positive integer (minimum `1`, never a float) counting the whole seconds until the current UTC minute window closes — terminated by a single newline. Repeating a limited request neither extends the window nor consumes budget, and the full budget of five returns automatically on the next UTC minute. The window opens with the scope's first valid request of that minute; the counter is persisted, so it is shared across processes and survives restarts, and concurrent acquisitions are exact — more than five simultaneous valid requests admit precisely five. No other endpoint (health, challenges, evidence, verification, decisions, grant minting, envelopes, trust roots, policies, rewrap, or the audit listings) is limited.

lines: - `POST /v1/rewrap-batches` rotates a page of envelopes within one tenant/workload scope without touching the single-envelope endpoint above. The JSON body must include non-empty `tenant_id` and `workload_id`, an optional integer `limit` (1–200, default 50) and an optional `cursor`. Each page selects that scope's envelopes in stable `data_id` order starting strictly after the cursor boundary; omitting the cursor (or sending an empty string) starts before the smallest `data_id`. Cursors are opaque, HMAC-authenticated tokens bound to their scope: a missing/blank/malformed value, wrong type, out-of-range `limit`, or a forged, tampered or cross-scope cursor returns `422`. Envelopes at historical key versions are unwrapped and re-wrapped under the current key one at a time (only `key_version` and `wrapped_key` change; body, IV, tag, identifier and `created_at` are untouched); envelopes already at the current version are recorded as `skipped` and change nothing. Each envelope is its own independent commit pairing the guarded material update with exactly one audit row recording the scope, envelope identifier, old/new key versions, a fixed result code (`rewrapped`/`skipped`) and a UTC timestamp — never the payload, data key, wrapped key or ciphertext. The compact, newline-free JSON response returns exactly `batch_id` (string), `processed`, `rewrapped`, `skipped`, `failed` (integers), `next_cursor` (string, empty at the end) and `complete` (boolean). A wholly invalid keyring is a server failure: the request returns `500`, creates no batch audit and modifies no envelope. If the keyring becomes unusable mid-page, a historical key is missing, or an individual rewrap fails, the page stops and the request still returns `200`: the failed envelope is left exactly as it was, gets one audit row with result `keyring`, `missing-key` or `rewrap`, `failed` is 1, and `next_cursor` stays before the failed item so a retry resumes there. Concurrent batches over the same scope advance each envelope at most once — the guarded update makes losers observe the already-current version as a skip, and replaying a `next_cursor` never re-wraps an envelope twice.
